q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this carefully.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-21. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release occurred on May 20, 2026 (according to the research provided). This means the resolution has **already occurred** — the guidance has already been announced. This is a retroactive forecasting question asking me to estimate what NVIDIA's forward guidance was at that time.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research explicitly states: **"NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%"**

This gives a range of:
- Floor: $89.2 billion ($91.0B × 0.98)
- Ceiling: $92.8 billion ($91.0B × 1.02)

The most likely outcome is the **midpoint of the guidance range: $91.0 billion**.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- If the actual reported guidance was at the conservative end of their ±2% range
- If there were unexpected supply chain constraints or demand softness not yet reflected
- If China restrictions became more severe after May 20, 2026 (though the guidance already excludes China revenue)

However, the research provides the actual guidance amount with high specificity ($91.0B ±2%), so the lower bound of the stated range would be $89.2B.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- If the company guided above the center of their stated range
- If demand remained stronger than expected
- If cost structures improved beyond expectations

However, the upper bound of the stated guidance range would be $92.8B.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- **Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion** (exceeded guidance)
- **Q2 FY2027 forward guidance: $91.0 billion ±2%** (this is the stated guidance)
- **Wall Street consensus: approximately $91.9 billion** (above NVIDIA's midpoint but within broader expectations)

The guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center revenue, which is a known constraint.

---

## Reasoning on the distribution

Since the guidance was explicitly provided as $91.0 billion plus or minus 2%, I should estimate the distribution around this announced midpoint:

- **Median (50th percentile):** The stated midpoint is $91.0 billion. This is the official guidance.
- **Low (10th percentile):** At the conservative end of the ±2% range: $89.2 billion
- **High (90th percentile):** At the optimistic end of the ±2% range: $92.8 billion

However, I should also consider that actual guidance numbers might have been slightly different from the standard ±2% presentation. Given that Wall Street consensus was slightly higher at ~$91.9B, and that Q1 beat guidance, there's a possibility the midpoint could have been guided slightly higher. But I'm anchoring to the explicitly stated $91.0B figure.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, is \$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This range puts the ceiling near \$92.8 billion and the floor near \$89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The company's outlook explicitly does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is approximately \$91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/) or \$91.846 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors), which falls within NVIDIA's guided range. For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported \$81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its own guidance [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
